channel.title: Protest Atlas
channel.description: National protests and strikes across Europe, checked daily.

item.title: Belgium: next protest Thursday 10 December
item.description: The union common front of the non-profit sector (social, health and culture, public and private) calls a national demonstration in Brussels on Thursday 10 December, starting at Brussels-North; no strike notice reported. At skeyes (air traffic control), the CSC Transcom and SLFP unions have filed a strike notice from 9 December; no strike date set (RTBF).

item.title: France: next protest Tuesday 1 December
item.description: Eight public-service unions call a national strike and day of action on Tuesday 1 December over pay, and the CGT, CFDT and UNSA invite private-sector workers to join; the government meets the unions again on 11 December. The Interfac Île-de-France student assembly calls a mobilisation on 26 November.

item.title: Greece: next protest Wednesday 25 November
item.description: ADEDY's 24-hour nationwide public-sector strike on Wednesday 25 November is joined by hospital staff, teachers, seafarers (no ferries from Attica ports), rail and metro staff and private-sector labour centres; the central rally is at Propylaia in Athens at 10:30, with rallies in more than 60 cities (ERT). Demands include pay rises, the 13th and 14th salaries and action on living costs and housing.

item.title: Croatia: next protest Saturday 12 December
item.description: The civic initiative "Vrijeme za promjene" has moved its anti-corruption protests in several cities (including Zagreb, Split, Rijeka, Osijek, Zadar and Pula) from 21 November to Saturday 12 December, citing safety and higher-than-expected interest; the youth strike organisers say they will continue.

item.title: Italy: next protest Friday 4 December
item.description: Grassroots unions (CUB, SGB, SI Cobas, Unicobas, ADL Varese, SBM, SGC) hold a 24-hour general strike across public and private sectors on Friday 4 December. The CGIL will join a health-sector demonstration in Rome on 5 December and holds a demonstration for the South in Cosenza on 12 December (Il Sole 24 Ore).

item.title: Netherlands: next protest Thursday 3 December
item.description: FNV and CNV announce further strikes in regional public transport (streekvervoer) on 3, 4, 14, 15 and 18 December, after strike days on 23 and 24 November.

item.title: Portugal: next protest Wednesday 25 November
item.description: The SMAQ train drivers' strike at CP continues with a second full stoppage on 25 November and runs until 27 November. The CGTP had called a rally outside parliament for the final 2027 budget vote on 24 November; no report of it found yet. No later national date announced in our sources yet.

item.title: Belgium: National demonstration in Brussels
item.description: Monday 23 November. 70,000 according to organisers, 50,000 official. Why: Wage indexation, Pensions, Spending cuts, VAT increase, Working time.

item.title: Portugal: Train drivers' strike at CP begins (23-27 November)
item.description: Monday 23 November. Turnout not reported. Why: Wages, Public services, Cost of living, Housing.

item.title: Austria: Youth strike: rallies in 14 cities, largest in Vienna
item.description: Friday 20 November. Turnout not reported. Why: University funding, Military spending, Education.

item.title: Switzerland: Nationwide youth strike with demonstrations in about ten cities
item.description: Friday 20 November. 40,000 according to organisers. Why: Military spending, Austerity, Education, Climate action.

item.title: Germany: Nationwide school strike and youth protests against conscription
item.description: Friday 20 November. 90,000 according to organisers. Why: Education, Cost of living, Military conscription, Climate, Health.

item.title: Croatia: Youth strike: class boycott and gatherings in about a dozen cities
item.description: Friday 20 November. Turnout not reported. Why: Cost of living, Housing, Corruption, Education & health.

item.title: Italy: CGIL general strike with marches in more than 100 cities
item.description: Friday 20 November. 1,500,000 according to organisers. Why: Wages & pensions, Cost of living, Budget law, Military spending.

item.title: Czechia: next protest Wednesday 2 December
item.description: Milion chvilek calls a nationwide "warning" action on Wednesday 2 December at 16:36 (signs in windows) and invites the cabinet to a public debate in Prague that evening.

item.title: Spain: 24-hour rail strike over safety across the network
item.description: Tuesday 17 November. Turnout not reported. Why: Housing, Wages, Rail safety after the Urda crash, Labour rights.

item.title: France: Public-sector strike day with marches across France
item.description: Tuesday 17 November. 500,000 according to organisers, 146,000 official. Why: Education funding & teacher shortages, Cost of living, Wages & minimum wage, Public services, Tax fairness.

item.title: Slovakia: "17 November for Change" opposition rallies on the Velvet Revolution anniversary
item.description: Tuesday 17 November. 25,000 according to organisers. Why: Opposition to the Fico government, Ties with Russia, Rule of law & freedoms.

item.title: Lithuania: Indefinite national teachers' strike begins
item.description: Monday 16 November. 4,000 according to organisers. Why: Teachers' pay.

item.title: Norway: Nationwide political strike for Posten with rallies at 40 locations
item.description: Monday 16 November. Turnout not reported. Why: Postal service cuts, Jobs.

item.title: Czechia: Milion chvilek rally on Letná plain, Prague
item.description: Sunday 15 November. 400,000 according to organisers. Why: Public media independence, Government accountability.

item.title: Netherlands: ANWB staff strike and union rally in The Hague
item.description: Monday 9 November. Turnout not reported. Why: Collective agreements.

item.title: Albania: National student protest in Tirana
item.description: Saturday 7 November. Turnout not reported. Why: Corruption, Education costs, Poor job prospects for young people.

item.title: Greece: Students and teachers rally for public education
item.description: Thursday 5 November. Turnout not reported. Why: Education funding, Housing & rents, Wages, Hospital staffing.

item.title: Denmark: Nationwide student strike and march in Copenhagen
item.description: Wednesday 4 November. 13,000 according to organisers. Why: Student grant (SU) cuts, Education funding.

item.title: Poland: Abortion-rights protests in 26 cities
item.description: Thursday 22 October. Turnout not reported. Why: Abortion rights.

item.title: Bulgaria: Rally outside the Presidency in Sofia
item.description: Tuesday 20 October. Turnout not reported. Why: A soft government response to attacks on ships in the Black Sea, blamed on Russia, Bulgaria's foreign policy toward Russia, 2027 budget: wages & pensions.

item.title: Ukraine: Rally against Kyiv's mayor
item.description: Saturday 17 October. Turnout not reported. Why: Kyiv city hall's poor preparation of heating and power for the winter.

item.title: Ireland: National 24-hour public sector strike
item.description: Wednesday 14 October. Turnout not reported. Why: Public sector pay.

item.title: United Kingdom: Pro-Palestine march in central London
item.description: Saturday 10 October. Turnout not reported. Why: NHS consultants' pay and conditions.

item.title: Kosovo: Protest in Pristina; police used tear gas and water cannon
item.description: Monday 5 October. Turnout not reported. Why: War-crimes verdicts (reported).
